title: Computer Use at the Edge of the Statistical Precipice — Pierluca D'Oro, Programma Labs
talk_summary: The speaker shows that deterministic benchmarks are gameable by 'replay agents' that blindly replay recorded successful traces, and that naive pass@K and rollout-only confidence intervals are statistically fragile. He proposes PRISM environment principles (multifactorial variation, verified configs, sandboxing, verifiers, realism) and hierarchical confidence intervals that account for both action and environment variance.

takeaways.technique: Replay-agent sanity check for eval suites
takeaways.what_they_do: They build a script that blindly replays recorded successful traces on the benchmark; if it scores near the frontier model, the benchmark is deterministic and gameable.
takeaways.numbers: Replay agent matches or beats frontier model on OSWorld/MobileWorld; script under 1MB for hundreds of tasks

takeaways.what_they_do: Vary initial state, data, theme, and starting screen per task, then run a compiler-like system that rejects invalid combinations so only verified configs are used.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can generate many configs all the combinations ... and you can then have a system that rejects the broken ones
takeaways.numbers: 387 verified scenarios expanded to 3.2M verified configurations

takeaways.technique: Hierarchical confidence intervals over rollouts and environment variation
takeaways.what_they_do: Compute confidence intervals that account for both action stochasticity (multiple rollouts) and environment variation, instead of rollout-only intervals.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you only use rollouts ... you have something like 17% on 20% coverage
takeaways.numbers: Rollout-only CIs achieve ~17-20% coverage vs nominal 95%; proper hierarchical method reaches 90-95%

takeaways.technique: Don't trust overconfident eval deltas for model selection
takeaways.what_they_do: Shows that small, overconfident confidence intervals lead to wrong model deployment decisions; a rigorous method says 'not confident enough, evaluate more'.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the method would tell to you um I'm not confident enough to make an informed decision
takeaways.numbers: 4% real performance mismatch × 1M tasks × ~$12-20 per mistake = hundreds of thousands per month

takeaways.what_they_do: Environment design checklist: multifactorial variation, verified combinations, sandboxing, privileged verifiers, faithful realism.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you want your environment to be sandboxed and you want uh your environment to support like verifiers

takeaways.technique: Measure robustness across variation axes, not just average score
takeaways.what_they_do: Reports worst-case performance across variation axes (initial screen, theme, data) rather than only mean success rate.
takeaways.evidence_quote: in the worst case frontier models are pretty bad actually at um being robust to these variations
